design_notes.note: The SW line is explicitly named as a noise source: the VOUT line must be connected to the output capacitor and routed AWAY from noisy components and traces (e.g. the SW line) or other noise sources. A layout that is not carefully done produces EMI problems and interference with RF circuits.

Input capacitor must be placed as close as possible to the IC pins VIN and GND, and the output capacitor close between VOUT and GND, to keep the switching current loop area small. Wide, short traces are required for the main current paths to provide a low inductance, low impedance ground path.

The exposed thermal pad and the GND pin must be connected; the exposed pad is not electrically connected to the IC but must be soldered and used as a central GND plane. This makes theta_JA and the return-current path the same design decision.

Once VIN falls close to VOUT the part enters no-ripple 100% mode: it stops switching entirely and connects the output to the input. Conducted switching emission therefore disappears at low battery voltage and is worst at high VIN, which is the opposite of most thermal worst cases.

provenance.notes: Output voltage ripple is NOT specified numerically anywhere in this datasheet -- it appears only as oscilloscope captures (Figures 23-27, pages 17-18) and as a qualitative 'low output ripple voltage' claim, so emissions.conducted[0].ripple is deliberately absent rather than read off a plot. di_dt is not stated. Only one theta_JA entry exists because the part ships in a single package (DSS/WSON-12) and TI's table gives no second copper-area condition; unlike the MCP73831 there is no large-copper alternate figure. Switching frequency is given only as an upper bound ('up to 2 MHz'), not as a typical fixed value, because DCS-Control is a quasi-fixed-frequency hysteretic topology; the fundamental drops with load current in Power Save Mode. Page numbers are PDF page numbers, which coincide with the printed page numbers in this document.
